latest.question: Deputy Shane Moynihan asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality whether, building on the childcare fee reductions announced in Budget 2027, consideration will be given to further supports for families on 50-hour contracts, particularly where providers do not offer shorter options.
latest.reply:
For a place for 50 or more hours per week, from September 2027 the maximum fee for a Core Funding Partner Service will be lowered from €336 per week to €300 per week. When combined with the increase in the Universal National Childcare Scheme subsidy, a family being charged the maximum fee for 50 or more hours (a “Band F” fee) and receiving 45 hours of subsidy, will save more than €52 per week, or more than €2,500 over 48 weeks.
The Government is committed to reduce parental fees to a maximum of €200 per month over the lifetime of the Government. Measures that will come into effect in September 2027 include both a lowering of fee caps for Core Funding Partner Services and increased National Childcare Scheme subsidies. As a result, many parents will see reductions in the amount they pay for early learning and childcare.
Later this year I will publish Shaping the Future Phase 2 which will set out the roadmap for how the €200 commitment will be achieved.
From September 2027, the maximum fees that early learning and childcare providers in receipt of Core Funding can charge will be reduced across all fee bands. All services with fees below the new caps will continue to be subject to existing fee controls.
Over €80 million is being allocated to support providers in adhering to this change to fee management conditions. The total allocation for year 6 of the scheme, commencing in September, is projected to exceed €650 million. This represents a 35% increase over year 5.

latest.question: Deputy Seán Kyne asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality for an update on the ten new family resource centres announced in Budget 2027; the current status of the process to establish these centres under consideration for allocation; and when their locations will be determined.
latest.reply:
The Programme for Government commits to work to increase funding and expand the capacity and network of Family Resource Centres. Budget 2027 honours this commitment. I was delighted to secure funding, as part of the Budget, for a further ten Family Resource Centres. This will bring Family Resource Centre Programme membership up to 146 members in 2027.
This further expansion of the Programme is the latest in several very positive developments for the Programme over the last few years. It follows the increase in the membership of the Programme in 2025 by five members, and in 2026 by a further ten members, bringing overall membership to its current 136 members. The establishment of ten new centres will be very welcome for the communities that will be served by these centres.
The most recent national application and assessment process for the Programme was undertaken in 2025. It was led by Tusla and independently chaired by a representative of the University of Limerick. This followed an open call for applications, with applications reviewed and scored against clearly defined and published criteria, including population need, level of deprivation, child population data, existing service provision and existing service gaps. Decisions on the successful services were made by an assessment panel.
I am aware that there continues to be a strong level of interest in communities around the country in having Family Resource Centres as part of their community infrastructure. This was borne

latest.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality if she will support extending paid paternity leave.
latest.reply:
There have been significant developments in entitlements for parents of working families in recent years. The Government is committed to supporting workers, including by extending paid leave for parents to allow them to spend more time with their child during their earliest years.
The Paternity Leave and Benefit Act 2016 provides the relevant parent (other than the mother of the child) with 2 weeks paid Paternity Leave Ireland's statutory Paternity Leave arrangements are fully aligned with the requirements of the EU Work-Life Balance Directive, which introduced a minimum standard for Paternity Leave across EU Member States.
Under the Parent’s Leave and Benefit Act 2019, working parents are also entitled to nine weeks of paid Parent's Leave for each relevant parent, to be taken in the first two years after the birth or adoptive placement of a child. Parent's Leave is an individual separate entitlement and is non-transferable between parents.
Under the Parental Leave (Amendment) Act 2019, an employee who is a relevant parent in respect of a child under the age 12 is entitled to 26 weeks’ unpaid Parental Leave for each child. Where a child has a disability or long-term illness, the entitlement can continue until the child is 16. A relevant parent is a parent, an adoptive parent, or a person acting in ‘loco parentis’. Both parents have an equal, separate entitlement to Parental Leave.

latest.question: Deputy Daniel Ennis asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality the way in which she and her Department are engaging in the cross-government network for the child poverty and well-being programme.
latest.reply:
It is important to recognise that given its multi-faceted nature, addressing child poverty requires a cross-government response. This is significant in terms of how the cross-government network on child poverty is in supporting Government Departments in addressing poverty and disadvantage.
In 2023, the Child Poverty and Well-being Programme Office in the Department of an Taoiseach established a Cross-Government Network to deepen cross-government coordination. The purpose of the Cross-Government Network on Child Poverty and Well-being overseen by the Department of an Taoiseach is to bring together a wide range of actors across government departments, their agencies, and local authorities who are responsible for implementing actions and policies which impact on the objective to end child poverty and enhance child well-being.
The network creates a platform to support this diverse work and helps to foster creativity and innovation as well as a shared purpose and mission. The Cross-Government Network has met eight times to date. Officials from across a range of relevant sections in the Department of Children, Disability and Equality have actively participated in the Cross-Government Network through conference and stakeholder events. I myself have attended the child poverty and well-being summits. With my fellow Ministers I have engaged with stakeholders at these meetings. It gives us an important opportunity to reflect on progress and identify where we need to do better.

latest.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality her plans to increase the numbers of frontline staff in disability services in County Louth.
latest.reply:
The HSE’s plans to increase frontline staffing in disability services in County Louth include the continued recruitment of approved 2026 posts, conversion of agency-funded roles to permanent staffing where appropriate, implementation of national and regional recruitment and retention initiatives, and delivery of additional workforce growth arising from Budget 2027 and the National Service Plan 2027.
County Louth forms part of the Louth/Meath Integrated Health Area (IHA) within the Dublin Northeast Health Region. Disability workforce data is reported on an IHA basis across both counties. Disaggregated data at county level is not readily available. The HSE has advised that the number of staff employed across HSE and section 38 disability services in Louth and Meath had reached 978 whole-time equivalents (WTEs) by end September, and the HSE expects it to reach its funded level by end 2026.
The HSE has allocated 22 New Service Development posts to disability services across Louth and Meath in 2026. These posts are primarily in frontline disciplines including Social Care Workers, Social Workers, Dietitians and Nursing. These staff support key service areas including Children’s Disability Network Teams (CDNTs) and Day Services. I understand that many of these posts have already been accepted with candidates in the process of being appointed, and the remaining posts are at advanced stages of recruitment.

latest.question: Deputy Seán Kyne asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality for an update on residential disability services in Galway; the steps being taken to increase residential capacity; and the details of additional residential places provided to date and those planned for Galway city and county in the future.
latest.reply:
The Department of Children, Disability and Equality continues to engage closely with the HSE on matters related to providing and expanding specialist disability residential services with a key focus on the increased emphasis for longer term planning of these vital services.
Budget 2027 delivers significant progress for disabled children and adults, bringing the budget for Disability Services to over €4billion for the first time. This will support the HSE, to provide a range of community services and supports to enable people with disabilities to live a life of their choosing.
While continuing to fund existing placements, this Budget will provide additional investment of €108.4million for residential services, which includes the full year cost of 2026 service delivery and a further expansion of services in 2027. This additional investment includes €62.4million for new developments.
Subject to finalisation of the HSE’s 2027 National Service Plan, this is expected to support a range of residential measures including 212 newly created placements as well as enhancements for existing residential places where individual needs have become more complex.
According to HSE data, as of September 2026, 9,048 specialist disability residential places are being delivered by approximately 90 service providers across the country. 1,506 of these places are being provided in the HSE West North West Region including 528 in County Galway.

The Government is committed to ensuring that children with disabilities and their families who need early intervention and therapy input can access that support in a timely way.
Children's Disability Network Teams provide services to children with complex needs arising from their disability under the progressing disability services model of service delivery.
The HSE provides the Department with CDNT service provision data at Regional Health Area level. According to June 2026 preliminary data 1,046 children are currently on the waitlist to access CDNT services in the Dublin and Midlands Regional Health Area.
Whilst recognising that there is more to do, real progress has been made in reducing the Children’s Disability Network Team waiting list. The overall HSE Disability Budget for 2027 has seen a growth to €4.1billion, which equates to a nearly 20% increase from the previous year.

latest.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality if she is concerned at the impact on children's rights of the use of a private company for supervised access resulting from court cases which has previously been barred from being used by Tusla due to concerns over its practices.
latest.reply:
In relation to this organisation, Tusla has confirmed that it has not commissioned its supervised access services since 8th October, 2024. Tusla has also taken additional steps to strengthen the controls in place to ensure that the company is not used again.
In a small number of cases, Tusla uses external providers, such as supervision and access centres, often at the direction of the courts. These services are typically used when a child is in the care of Tusla.
Regarding the commissioning of services by Tusla, a process exists for all external third-party providers, to register with Tusla. This involves a governance process, including confirmation of qualifications, Garda vetting, mandatory training, and membership of relevant professional bodies, among other checks.
Regarding safeguarding and the rights of the child, all organisations, including private supervised access services, are duty bound to follow Children First: National Guidance for the Protection and Welfare of Children (2017). This is the primary statutory policy framework designed to help organisations identify, report, and manage concerns regarding the safety and welfare of children.
Under Children First, supervision/access centres are classified as a 'relevant service' as they provide care and supervision of children whilst in the centre. Regarding the future use of the St Mary of the Angels campus, as the Deputy will be aware, the campus is not owned by the HSE or the Department of Children, Disability and Equality. Rather, it should be noted that it is owned and operated by St John of God Community Services Limited.

latest.question: Deputy Conor D. McGuinness asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality to provide an update on the childcare providers who have received proposed commercial rates valuations that threaten the viability of their services.
latest.reply:
The majority of early learning and childcare providers operating on a for-profit basis are liable for commercial rates, as they do not qualify for the not-for-profit exemption under Schedule 4 of the Valuation (Amendment) Act 2015.
Paragraph 22 of the Schedule provides that early childhood care and education facilities that are established and operated on a not-for-profit basis are exempt from rates; it does not provide a general exemption from rates for all childcare or childminding facilities operating on a for-profit basis. To avoid ambiguity, if an early childhood care and education facility is established and operated on a for-profit basis, then it does not fulfil the criteria for exemption under Paragraph 22.
The Department, and others, have previously advised the sector that ECCE-only services are exempt from paying commercial rates under Paragraph 10, Schedule 4 of the Valuation Act 2001. However, I am aware that a number of ECCE-only services have been receiving rates-payable notifications from their Local Authorities.
Given the importance of early learning and childcare for children, families and communities across the country, I am giving this matter my full attention.
I have engaged with my cabinet colleague, Minister Browne, on this matter, and I am hopeful that a satisfactory conclusion can be reached.

latest.question: Deputy Matt Carthy asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment if he, or his senior officials, have had meetings with the national waste collection permit office since March 2025.
latest.reply:
The National Waste Collection Permit Office (NWCPO), hosted by Offaly County Council, is the designated Nominated Authority for the processing and review of all waste collection permits issued within the State.
The Department is in regular contact with the NWCPO including meetings, fora and steering committees to discuss topics including, but not limited to, the operation of the waste collection market in Ireland, Waste Recovery Levy collection, and implementation of relevant actions in the Waste Action Plan for a Circular Economy.
The Waste Action Plan for a Circular Economy (WAPCE) contains a commitment to introduce further measures to incentivise the prevention and segregation of waste.
Arising from this commitment, the National Waste Collection Permit Office commissioned an independent study on incentivised waste charging and its potential implementation through the Waste Collection Permitting System. Officials from the Department were part of the steering group for the study.
This study, which has been shared with the Department, examines what changes could be made to the permitting system for waste collectors to fully incentivise waste prevention and improve source segregation practices by their customers to minimise their waste collection bills.

latest.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality the actions her Department is taking to strengthen the rights of non-binary people.
latest.reply:
As Minister for Children, Disability and Equality, responsibility for gender recognition does not come within my remit. Matters relating to the legal recognition of gender, including any consideration of the recognition of non-binary identities, come within the remit of the Minister for Social Protection and of the Department of Social Protection.
However, I do have responsibility for the Government's overall policy on LGBTIQ+ matters. The Department of Children, Disability and Equality coordinates implementation of the cross-government National LGBTIQ+ Inclusion Strategy II 2024-2028. The Strategy, together with its first Action Plan 2025–2026, provides a roadmap for advancing equality for LGBTIQ+ people in Ireland. The Strategy places a particular focus on addressing the experiences and needs of the most marginalised groups within the LGBTIQ+ community. The LGBTIQ+ Community Services Fund is a key element of this Strategy. Yesterday, I announced the opening of the 2027 LGBTIQ+ Community Services Fund for applications. In 2027, €2 million is being made available to applicant groups, operating at national, regional, and local level, to promote inclusion and protect the rights of LGBTIQ+ people in Ireland.
While significant progress has been made in advancing the rights of LGBTIQ+ people, the Strategy recognises that legislative gaps remain in a number of areas and includes commitments to examine and address these where appropriate.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.
